title: iOACAM Observation Event
description: The single message type emitted by any perception or telemetry source and consumed by the workflow engine. This is the contract boundary: the engine never sees pixels, models, or sensor internals, only events in this form.

event_id.description: Unique id for this event. UUIDv4 or a monotonic per-source counter. Used for de-duplication and for referencing the event from a log entry or SOC alert.

timestamp_us.description: Monotonic device clock in microseconds since boot. Monotonic, NOT wall clock, so that NTP corrections cannot reorder or duplicate events. Wall clock is recorded separately at log-write time.

wall_time.description: Optional UTC wall-clock time, for human-readable logs and SOC correlation only. Never used for sequencing or timer logic.

source.description: Which subsystem produced this event. Determines whether the event carries genuine uncertainty. Camera and radar events are inferred and carry confidence < 1.0. Bus, access_control and timer events are read or computed facts and carry confidence = 1.0.

sensor_id.description: Which physical sensor instance produced this event, e.g. 'cam-01', 'radar-01', 'plc-line3'. Required for camera and radar sources so that per-sensor calibration and per-camera false-alarm rates can be measured.

track_id.description: Tracker-assigned id, stable for as long as one subject remains continuously tracked by one sensor. Used to accumulate persistence and to associate a sequence of observations with one actor. Absent for events with no tracked subject, e.g. environment readings.

observation.description: What was observed. This is a CLOSED list, deliberately. Adding an entry means committing to a detector for it, a feasibility assessment, and an ATP test. Do not extend it casually; anything outside this list is what the 'unknown' verdict exists for.

subject.description: Who or what the observation is about. Populate as much as is known; unknown fields are omitted rather than guessed. A subject with no identity but a known role (from a badge-in in the same zone) is still fully usable by role-based rules.

class.description: Actor class. Drives which branch of the policy applies. 'nature' events are routed to the safety path, not the SOC security path.

identity.description: Enrolled identity if recognised, e.g. 'EMP-4471'. Omitted when the subject is present but unidentified.

role.description: Role such as 'operator', 'maintenance_engineer', 'visitor'. May be known from the access control event even when face recognition did not identify the person.

asset_id.description: For machine, robot and object subjects, e.g. 'robot-cell-3', 'torque-wrench-12'.

zone_id.description: Site zone in which the observation occurred, e.g. 'zone-assembly-4', 'zone-robot-cell-3'. Zones are declared in the site configuration. Most policy rules key on this.

value.description: The observed value. Its type depends on the observation: boolean for presence and PPE, integer for counts, string for states and recognised actions, number for environment levels.

unit.description: Unit for numeric values, e.g. 'metres', 'celsius', 'm_per_s'. Required whenever value is a number so that thresholds are unambiguous.

confidence.description: Calibrated confidence that this observation is correct, after quality discounting, persistence and sensor agreement. Exactly 1.0 for events derived from a bus read, an access control transaction, or a timer, because those carry no perception uncertainty.

confidence_components.description: The factors that produced 'confidence', retained separately so that a site engineer tuning thresholds can tell a genuinely ambiguous detection apart from a good detection made under poor viewing conditions. Optional in production, mandatory during commissioning and ATP.

raw_score.description: The model's uncalibrated output, before temperature scaling. Recorded so calibration drift is detectable without re-running the model.

calibrated_score.description: raw_score after the site's temperature scaling correction.

quality.description: Viewing-condition factor derived from subject pixel height, occlusion fraction, detected keypoint count, motion blur and scene luminance. Computed without AI.

persistence.description: How consistently the same result held across the tracking window. A flickering result scores low.

agreement.description: Cross-sensor agreement adjustment, capped. Sensors that fail for a common cause are not treated as independent.

frames_observed.description: Number of frames contributing to this event.

evidence_ref.description: Pointer to the retained evidence for this event. Evidence is only persisted for events that reach an operator; conformant events keep no media. Kept as a reference rather than inline so the event stream stays small.

clip_id.description: Id of the retained clip in the encrypted rolling buffer.

clip_start_us.description: Monotonic start time of the retained window.

clip_end_us.description: Monotonic end time of the retained window.

skeleton_only.description: True when only pose keypoints were retained rather than video. Preferred default: it satisfies most investigation needs while substantially reducing the privacy and retention burden.

integrity.description: Tamper-evidence fields. The engine chains events so that a deleted or altered event breaks the chain. Required for the defence and aerospace use cases and for the forensic value of the log.

seq.description: Monotonic counter per source. A gap means events were lost or removed.

prev_hash.description: Hash of the previous event from this source, forming the chain.

signature.description: Signature over the event, keyed from the TPM. Applied at log-write time, not per event in the hot path.
